properties.name: Peter (Simon Peter)
properties.bioIntro: Simon Peter was a Galilean fisherman who became one of Jesus's closest disciples and a leading voice in the early church.
bioBullets: A fisherman from Capernaum on the Sea of Galilee
Called by Jesus to leave his nets and follow him
Part of Jesus's inner circle of three, alongside James and John
Given the name "Peter" ("the rock") by Jesus
Denied knowing Jesus three times before the crucifixion
Restored by Jesus after the resurrection
Preached the first public sermon of the church at Pentecost
Traditional death c. AD 64 under Nero's persecution — this comes from early church history, not Scripture itself

route.name: Called as a disciple
route.story: While preaching by the Sea of Galilee, Jesus borrowed Peter's boat to teach the crowd. Afterward he told Peter to cast his nets again — after a fruitless night, they came up overflowing with fish. Stunned, Peter left everything to follow Jesus.

route.name: Declares Jesus the Messiah
route.story: Near Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asked who the disciples believed he was. Peter answered that he was the Messiah, the Son of God. Jesus affirmed Peter's insight, renamed him "Peter" (the rock), and said his church would be built on this declaration.

route.name: Denies knowing Jesus
route.story: After Jesus's arrest, Peter followed at a distance into the high priest's courtyard. Three separate times he denied knowing Jesus — just as Jesus had predicted. When a rooster crowed after the third denial, Peter realized what he had done and wept bitterly.
route.locationNote: Pinned to the Church of St. Peter in Gallicantu, the traditional (not scripturally specified) site of the high priest's house.

route.name: Restored by Jesus
route.story: After the resurrection, Jesus met the disciples again by the Sea of Galilee. He asked Peter three times if he loved him — mirroring Peter's three denials — and each time told him to care for his followers. It was a public restoration and a commissioning to lead.

route.name: Preaches at Pentecost
route.story: Fifty days after the resurrection, the Holy Spirit came upon the disciples in Jerusalem. Peter stood and preached to the crowd that Jesus was the promised Messiah, raised from the dead. About 3,000 people believed that day, marking the beginning of the church.
route.locationNote: Pinned to the Cenacle (Upper Room), the traditional (not scripturally specified) site of Pentecost.
